$comment: Sea battle tuning (PRD sections 9.1 and 9.6). Every number a fight turns on lives here: battle pace and map, gun arcs, ranges, reloads and hit chances, what each ammo does, when a ship strikes, boarding strength, how each kind of captain fights, and what a fight does to standing. autoResolve: a fight between AI ships is settled by crew x (1 + guns/10) x the role's factor; the winner loses `losses` of her crew. Who sails her (slice 1a of docs/design/combat-model.md): an AI ship's crew is green, regular, seasoned or veteran ('crewQuality': multiples of reload time, shot scatter and boarding strength), and her captain has gunnery, seamanship, boarding and resolve from 0 to 100, drawn at spawn from her role's ranges ('captains', crew grades by weight). At 50 a skill changes nothing; at 100 gunnery cuts reload by half of 'skill.reload' and scatter by half of 'skill.spread', boarding adds half of 'skill.boarding' to boarding strength, and seamanship has her rethink every 'skill.thinkTicks' ticks (12 at 0 down to 4 at 100; 8 at 50). A ship with none of this (the player's) fights as a regular crew under a captain of 50. Doctrine and surrender (slice 1b): what each role fires ('doctrines': round at the hull; chain at the rigging; 'pirate' chain, then grape at grape range, to take her whole), French patrols chain, Spanish patrols' soldiers make them 'boardingDefence' times harder to board. A beaten ship strikes each second at strike.chance, more or less by her captain's resolve (up to half of strike.resolve either way), her crew's morale against her role's usual, and the odds against her (her opponent's men x guns over hers, 0.5 to 2, to the power strike.oddsWeight). A famous pirate calls on the player to strike when her boarding odds fall below strike.demandOdds or her hull below strike.demandHull, within strike.demandTiles: striking gives up the plunder chest and the hold and keeps the ship and her men. Guns and range (slice 4): a ball's power falls from full within guns.pointBlank of her reach to guns.longShotPower at its end (hull, sails and men alike); a ball flying down her length (its line within 'raking.cos' of her heading) rakes her for 'raking.damage' times the harm; swivel guns (her class's 'swivels', and the fit) sweep the deck of a ship within 'swivels.tiles' every 'swivels.everySeconds', 'swivels.crewPer' men a swivel; chasers (her class's 'chasers') fire one round shot each from bow or stern every 'chasers.everySeconds' at a ship within 'chasers.arcDeg' of her head or stern and within reach. Difficulty (slice 6): five levels ('difficulty.levels', picked for a new career; 'default' when none is) move only the opponents and the battle, never the player's own ship or any ship's speed: 'skill' is added to every AI captain's skills as drawn, 'crew' moves a drawn crew a grade better (above 0) or worse (below 0) at that chance, 'fits' multiplies each role's chance of carrying each fit, 'windShiftDeg' veers the battle wind up to that many degrees either way every 'windShiftSeconds', 'nearMissTiles' widens the enemy's hull by that much for the player's balls, and 'notice' multiplies the strength a famous pirate waits for before he hunts the player.

masts.$comment: Rigging hits wear down the nearest mast (strength 100); a fallen mast takes its share of canvas and a few men. Chain is aimed high.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.about: Green crews under timid captains, few fitted ships, a steady wind, near misses count as hits, and the famous pirates wait until you are much stronger.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.about: Easier crews and captains, fewer fits, a steady wind, near misses sometimes count, and the famous pirates notice you a little later.

levels.name: Adventurer
levels.about: The Caribbean as it was tuned: crews, captains and fits as drawn, a steady wind in battle.

levels.name: Rogue
levels.about: Better crews and sharper captains, more fitted ships, the wind shifts in battle, and the famous pirates notice you sooner.

levels.name: Swashbuckler
levels.about: Seasoned crews under the best captains, well-fitted ships, a wind that veers through a fight, and the famous pirates come for you early.

shipyard.$comment: Ships for sale at a shipwright (PRD section 7), by the port's size: a hamlet builds none, a town the small ones, a city most. The great ships (the ship of the line, the galleons) are built in Europe: the only way to one is to take her. A ship bought comes new, at her class's price, with 'gunsShare' of her battery mounted (more at 150 gold a gun).

prizes.$comment: Ships that change hands: a pirate who wins keeps the beaten ship in tow (up to 'max'), her hold adding to hers and her pace holding her back; she sells them at her haven 'sellDays' after taking them. Beaten by a pirate, the player loses the most valuable ship of the fleet (never the flagship). A ship of the player's freed by a patrol lies at that nation's nearest port, to be taken back for 'salvage' of her value.

news.blockade: {nation} warships are lying off {town}: little gets in or out.
news.yourShipTaken: The pirate {ship} took your {vessel} off {town}, and is making for her haven.
news.prizeSold: The pirate {ship} has sold the {vessel} at {town}.
